title: What If You Stood in Death Valley on Its Hottest Day?

scenes.text: What if you stood in Death Valley on its hottest day? The air isn't the worst part.
The official world record is 134 degrees, set in 1913, though some experts now doubt it.
Even doubters accept 130 degrees, measured by a sensor in 2020, and again in 2021.
But the ground is worse. In 1972 it hit 201 degrees while the air was only 128.
Above 120 degrees, rescue helicopters may not be able to fly, so help can't just drop in.
You'd stand 190 feet below sea level, on ground hotter than any air ever measured.

description:
